ig_caption:
May 1997, New York. A computer beat the world champion.

In February 1996, IBM's Deep Blue won the first game of its match with Garry Kasparov, but Kasparov took the match 4–2. The rematch came fifteen months later. After five games it was level at 2½–2½. In game six, a Caro-Kann, Deep Blue gave a knight on e6 on move 8, and Black resigned after 19.c4.

Final score: 3½–2½. The first time a computer had beaten a reigning world champion in a match under tournament conditions.

slides.title: Round one went to the human
slides.body: In February 1996, IBM's Deep Blue played world champion Garry Kasparov over six games. It won game one: the first classical game a computer had won against a reigning world champion.

slides.title: The rematch
slides.body: Fifteen months later they met again over six games. After five, the score was level: one win each and three draws.
slides.note: Everything came down to game six, on 11 May 1997.

slides.title: Game six
slides.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Ng5 Ngf6 Bd3 e6 N1f3 h6 Nxe6
slides.take: A Caro-Kann, with Kasparov as Black. On move 8 Deep Blue gave a knight on e6 to break open the cover around Black's king.
slides.edge: Black's king had to walk to d8, then c8, while White's pieces came in.
